title: Thick cylinder benchmark (TL × SVK × Hex8)
objective: Run a thick-walled internally-pressurised cylinder benchmark and compare radial displacement and hoop stress to the Lamé closed-form solution at several radii.
scope: Build a quarter-cylinder mesh (symmetry BCs on the two radial faces, internal pressure on the inner radius).
Run with SVK and TL Hex8.
Extract radial displacement u_r(r) at a few radial sample points and compare to the Lamé solution.
implementation_steps: Derive or paste the Lamé closed-form.
Run the simulation and extract radial displacements.
acceptance_criteria: Radial displacement matches Lamé within 2% at 5 sample radii.
risks: Curved geometry with Hex8 is lossy; hoop stress gradients may be noisy near the inner radius. Mitigation: refine mesh near r = r_inner.
completion_notes: Pathfinder for mechdsl.verify.benchmarks (P10-6/8/9 reuse BenchmarkResult + element_cauchy_stress).
Quarter-cylinder mesh 24 radial x 20 angular x 1 axial (plane-strain via u_z=0 on both z-faces, radial bias 1.05).
Max u_r rel-err 0.81% (spec: <2%); max sigma_theta_theta rel-err 1.75% (spec: <3%). Newton 3 iters, ~55s wallclock.
Gate A notes: element_cauchy_stress reachable via mechdsl.verify.benchmarks._core; expose in __init__.py when P10-6/8/9 land.
Gate B advisory: centroid hoop-stress sampling uses parametric centroid not geometric centroid; acceptable here, worth documenting for P10-8 damage task.
